metadata.title: Le Chatelier: Disturbance, Shift, New Balance
metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.objective: Show how a concentration or temperature change shifts a reversible equilibrium.
misconceptions: The equilibrium constant changes with concentration
expectedUnderstanding: A concentration change shifts the balance without changing K at fixed temperature
A temperature change can change K
Forward and reverse rates are equal but nonzero at equilibrium

primitives.text: Le Chatelier: A ⇌ B at equilibrium
K = [B]/[A]; at equilibrium forward rate = reverse rate, not zero.
Adding A shifts the balance right; at fixed T, K is unchanged. Heating changes K.
Rates balance at equilibrium, so the reaction does not stop. Both rate bars stay nonzero.

checkpoints.title: Balance, not rest
checkpoints.body: At the start, the forward and reverse rates are equal and both are nonzero. Equilibrium is dynamic: A still becomes B and B still becomes A at matching rates.

checkpoints.title: Add reactant A
checkpoints.body: Adding A raises the forward rate above the reverse rate. The beam tilts and B begins to build. At fixed temperature, the equilibrium constant K does not change.

checkpoints.title: The balance point shifts
checkpoints.body: A is consumed and B accumulates. The reaction quotient moves toward K, so the balance point shifts to the right. The K bar stays fixed because only temperature changes K here.

checkpoints.title: A new equilibrium
checkpoints.body: Forward and reverse rates converge again. The mixture reaches a new equilibrium with more B. The bar lengths are still nonzero, and K is the same as before at this temperature.

checkpoints.title: Heat changes K itself
checkpoints.body: Raise the temperature. The K bar changes because K depends on temperature; the final A and B amounts change too. A concentration change shifted the balance, but only a temperature change altered K.

narration.text: At equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates.
Adding A raises the forward rate and tilts the balance toward B.
B builds as A is consumed. The balance point shifts, but K stays fixed at this temperature.
The rates meet again at a new equilibrium with more B.
Temperature changes K itself; a concentration change only shifts the balance point.

fallback.text: A reversible reaction A ⇌ B has equilibrium constant K = [B]/[A]. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, but both remain nonzero, so the reaction has not stopped. Adding reactant A raises the forward rate above the reverse rate; A is consumed and B builds until the rates meet again at a new equilibrium with more B. At fixed temperature, this concentration change shifts the balance point but does not change K. A temperature change can change K itself: in this endothermic-forward example, raising temperature increases K and produces more B at the new equilibrium. Concentration changes and temperature changes therefore act differently, and equilibrium is a dynamic balance of rates rather than a static stop.

accessibility.alt: A balance beam and forward/reverse rate bars show A to B. Adding A tilts the beam, builds B, then equal rates return. Sliders change added A and temperature; K stays fixed with concentration but moves with temperature.
